notes:
POC focus: enterprise Dedicated capacity evaluation. Short, practical notes from calls and experiments:
- Workloads: mixed — primary chat agent (low-latency, 120–200 token responses), reranking pipeline (batch, top-10 -> top-1 scoring), embeddings for semantic search (small vectors), occasional long-form summarization (1k+ tokens).
- Targets: p50 < 40ms per token, p95 < 120ms, p99 < 300ms for chat with 128-token responses under steady state. Reranking throughput target 60 qps (end-to-end top-5), embedding throughput 300 qps (small vectors). Sustained concurrency target: 450 simultaneous sessions.
- Reserved GPU planning: Luminar expects pricing for commits at 8x H100 equiv. baseline with headroom options (+25% burst capacity). Preferred configs discussed: 8x H100 (low-latency), alternative 12x A100 for cost-first. Redwood to provide GPU mapping and per-GPU throughput guidance.
- Load/Soak plan: 24h ramp (0 -> 150% target), 72h soak at 100% with scheduled fault injection (node restart, network partition), final 8h peak stress to validate autoscaling and burst behavior. Metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99, CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, token/sec, cold-start latency, GPU memory headroom, queue lengths.
- Representative prompts (samples provided in Drive):
  * Chat short: "Agent: Help me reconcile transaction 0xB3C — explain differences between ledger and bank file (120 tokens)."
  * Rerank: 10 candidate answers, need top-1 in <200ms end-to-end for scoring model.
  * Summarization: 3k-word earnings transcript -> 3-paragraph summary (target generation length 800–1200 tokens).
  * Embedding: 128-d vector for ~512-byte doc chunk.
- Acceptance criteria (POC): p99 latency <= 300ms for chat at steady state; reranking 95th percentile end-to-end < 250ms; no data residency violation; sustained GPU utilization 65–85% with ability to absorb 25% burst without major latency degradation.
- SLA negotiation points: define latency SLOs per workload class, credits for misses (sliding scale), minimum reserved capacity guarantee and on-demand burst SLAs, rollback/fallback model options, escalation path and RTO for critical outages, SOC2 + monthly audit log exports. Luminar likely will ask for contract clause capping overage spend and clear billing for burst consumption.
- Security: must support customer KMS (bring-your-own key) for model inputs/outputs at rest, SAML SSO for admin console, per-token audit logs for at least 90 days, option for EU data residency for a subset of data.
- Pricing sensitivity: moderate — willing to commit to 12-month reserved plan if unit economics are inside target; request breakpoints at 6/12/24 months and clear overage rates.
- Quotes from execs: "If p99 isn't under 300ms we can't go live — latency is a gating factor" (Head of Product).
- Known risks: internal ML infra team may push for self-hosting if Redwood Dedicated cannot meet cost targets; security team's backlog delays KMS integration; burst billing unclear to finance.
- Next actions (owners):
  * Redwood to deliver full soak test report + per-GPU throughput matrix (owner: Priya) by 2025-02-25.
  * Legal + Luminar to align on preliminary SLA terms; redlines expected after exec review (owner: Jordan).
  * InfraSec to validate KMS flow with sample encryption keys and provide sign-off checklist by 2025-02-28 (owner: Luminar Sec lead).
  * Schedule 30m exec review week of 2025-02-26 — confirm final ARR band and commit length.
